questions.q: What makes a GitHub Actions workflow file a reusable workflow that other workflows can call?
options: It declares on: workflow_call in place of a normal trigger like push
Naming the file reusable.yml
Adding a workflow_dispatch trigger to it
Storing it inside a .github/templates folder
questions.explain: A reusable workflow is a normal workflow file whose trigger is on: workflow_call, which is what lets another workflow call it with a uses: line.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend pinning a consumer repo to a reusable workflow's @v1 tag instead of @main?
options: @main is not valid syntax for calling a reusable workflow
Tags execute faster than branches inside GitHub Actions runners
Pinning to a tag keeps the consumer's build reproducible and immune to new commits landing on the template's default branch
@v1 is required by GitHub before secrets can be inherited
questions.explain: Pinning to a tagged release means the consuming pipeline's behavior can't change just because someone pushed a new commit to the template repo's default branch.

questions.q: In the Azure DevOps example, what does the extends keyword guarantee that a plain step-level template include does not?
options: That the pipeline only runs on Windows-hosted agents
That parameters can never be customized by the consumer
That the template repository is forked automatically
That the consuming pipeline cannot silently skip the steps the template defines
questions.explain: extends is a stronger structural guarantee than a step-level template include — a consumer pipeline built with extends can't quietly drop the steps a required template defines.

questions.q: What problem does baking a required security scan step directly into the shared pipeline template solve?
options: It removes the need for any security scanning tool entirely
The scan step becomes part of what every consumer gets by default, instead of something a team has to remember to add
It automatically remediates any vulnerabilities the scan finds
It eliminates the need for a dedicated templates repository
questions.explain: Putting the required scan step inside the template itself means every repo that calls the template gets it automatically, rather than relying on each team to remember a manual policy.

questions.q: What does the lesson say a healthy pipeline template should do as more teams start depending on it?
options: Expose a small set of explicit, well-named inputs and leave everything else as a sane default, rather than piling on one-off conditionals
Add a new if-branch inside the template for every team's specific quirks
Require every team to fork the template for their own use case
Remove all inputs so the template behaves identically for every caller
questions.explain: A healthy template stays maintainable by exposing a deliberate, small set of inputs instead of accumulating special-case conditionals for individual teams.
